"Center Court: On Our Radar," ''Basketball Times'', October 2018.] Retrieved October 8, 2022. born October 8, 1996) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for [[Hapoel Jerusalem B.C.|Hapoel Jerusalem]] of the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League|Israeli Premier League]] and the [[EuroCup Basketball|EuroCup]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[UNC Wilmington Seahawks men's basketball|UNC Wilmington Seahawks]], where in the [[2017–18 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2017–18 season]] he led the nation in rebounding. ==Early life== Cacok was born in [[Chicago|Chicago, Illinois]] to a Haitian-American father Harry Cacok and Rose Lewis,{{Cite web|url=https://uncwsports.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=6203|title=Devontae Cacok – Men's Basketball|website=uncwsports.com|access-date=June 26, 2019}} and grew up in [[Riverdale, Georgia]], playing football as a youth, mainly on the offensive line. He first began playing basketball in eight grade after he fractured his wrist, ending his football season. Cacok admits being terrible at first, but joined his high school varsity team after a seven-inch growth spurt as a sophomore. As a senior at [[Alpharetta High School]], he averaged 22 points and 12 rebounds per game and led the team to a 2nd place regional finish.{{cite news|last1=Fuchs|first1=Jeremy|title=He Made More of His Shots Last Year Than Anyone. Now Devontae Cacok Wants You to Know His Name|url=https://www.si.com/college-basketball/2017/10/26/devontae-cacok-uncw-seahawks-field-goal-percentage|access-date=April 29, 2018|work=[[Sports Illustrated]]|date=October 26, 2017}} ==College career== As a freshman at UNC Wilmington, Cacok came off the bench to average 3.3 points per game. Cacok averaged 12.2 points and 9.8 rebounds per game as a sophomore and led the nation in field goal percentage (80.0%). He accomplished this extremely high percentage, the highest ever, by mainly shooting within a range of about two feet from the basket and only taking one jump shot all year on the 29–6 Seahawks team. He had 40 blocks and tied for the league lead with 11 double-doubles. He was named [[Colonial Athletic Association|CAA]] Defensive Player of the Year and was selected to the Third Team All-CAA.{{cite press release|url=http://caasports.com/news/2017/3/2/MBB_0302174721.aspx |title=Williams headlines All-CAA men's basketball team |publisher=Colonial Athletic Association |date=March 2, 2017 |access-date=March 3, 2017}} After the season, UNC Wilmington lost four starters and coach [[Kevin Keatts]]; new coach [[C. B. McGrath]] looked to expand his overall game. In an 87–63 win against [[Elon Phoenix men's basketball|Elon]] in February 2018, Cacok posted 17 points and 21 rebounds. The following matchup, an 88–64 loss to [[College of Charleston Cougars men's basketball|College of Charleston]], he had 29 points and 17 rebounds. These two performances earned him CBS Sports Player of the Week honors.{{cite news|last1=Norlander|first1=Matt|title=Player of the Week: UNCW's Devontate Cacok almost sees a 20–20 average|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/player-of-the-week-uncws-devontate-cacok-almost-sees-a-20-20-average/|access-date=April 29, 2018|work=[[CBS Sports]]|date=February 21, 2018}} As a junior, Cacok led Division I in rebounding with 13.5 per game.{{cite web|title=Rebounds Per Game|url=https://www.ncaa.com/stats/basketball-men/d1/current/individual/137|website=NCAA|access-date=April 29, 2018}} He finished eighth in the CAA in scoring with 17.8 points per game and third in field goal percentage with 58.8%. Cacok led the conference with 22 double-doubles, second-most of any player in the country. He was named to the First Team All-CAA.{{cite web|last1=Washburn|first1=Rob|title=WRIGHT-FOREMAN TOPS ALL-CAA MEN'S {{sic|nolink=y|reason=error in source|BASEKTBALL}} TEAM|url=http://caasports.com/news/2018/3/1/mens-basketball-wright-foreman-tops-all-caa-mens-basektball-team.aspx?path=mbball|website=caasports.com|publisher=Colonial Athletic Association|access-date=April 29, 2018|date=March 2, 2018}} The North Carolina Collegiate Sports Information Association named Cacok to the First Team All-State.{{cite news|last1=Smist|first1=John|title=Devontae Cacok and Jordon Talley take home NCCSIA honors|url=http://www.fox19.com/story/37924796/devontae-cacok-and-jordon-talley-take-home-nccsia-honors|access-date=April 29, 2018|work=Fox 19|date=April 10, 2018|archive-date=April 30, season, Cacok was named to the Preseason First Team All-CAA.{{Cite web|url=https://caasports.com/news/2018/10/16/northeastern-favored-to-win-caa-mens-basketball-championship.aspx|title=NORTHEASTERN FAVORED TO WIN CAA MEN'S BASKETBALL CHAMPIONSHIP|website=CAA Sports|language=en|date=October 17, 2018|access-date=October 19, 2018}} As a senior, Cacok averaged 15.2 points and 12.3 rebounds per game and led the nation in double-doubles with 22.{{cite news |last1=Smist |first1=John |title=UNCW's Devontae Cacok makes NCAA history |url=https://www.wect.com/2019/04/26/uncws-devontae-cacok-makes-ncaa-history/ |access-date=December 16, 2019 |work=WECT |date=April 26, 2019}} He was again selected to the First Team All-CAA.{{cite news |title=CofC's Brantley and Riller Earn A Spot On The All-CAA First Team |url=https://www.live5news.com/2019/03/08/cofcs-brantley-riller-earn-spot-all-caa-first-team/ |access-date=December 16, 2019 |work=Live 5 News |date=March 8, 2019}} ==Professional career== ===Los Angeles Lakers (2019–2021)=== After going undrafted in the [[2019 NBA draft]], Cacok signed an Exhibit 10 contract with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] to play in the [[2019 NBA Summer League]].{{Cite news|url=https://247sports.com/nba/los-angeles-lakers/Article/Lakers-reportedly-sign-several-rookies-for-Summer-League-133071102/|title=Lakers reportedly sign several rookies for Summer Holman|url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/190709-lakers-sign-cacok-holman|website=NBA.com|access-date=July 10, 2019|date=July 9, 2019}} On October 21, 2019, Cacok was waived by the Lakers.{{cite web|title=Lakers Waive Cacok and Jackson |url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/lakers-waive-cacok-and-jackson|website=NBA.com|access-date=October 21, 2019|date=October 21, 2019}} He was then added to the roster of the [[South Bay Lakers]] of the [[NBA G League]].{{cite news |title= South Bay Lakers Set Opening Night Roster |url= https://southbay.gleague.nba.com/news/south-bay-lakers-set-opening-night-roster-1920/ |access-date= November 7, 2019 |work= [[NBA.com]] |date= November 4, 2019 |archive-date= January 21, 2021 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20210121012818/https://southbay.gleague.nba.com/news/south-bay-lakers-set-opening-night-roster-1920/ |url-status= dead }} On December 11, 2019, Cacok signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]], where he would split time between South Bay and LA.{{cite web |title= Lakers Sign Devontae Cacok to Two-Way Contract |url= https://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/lakers-sign-devontae-cacok-two-way-contract |website=NBA.com |access-date=December 11, 2019}} On December 28, 2019, Cacok grabbed a career-high 19 rebounds to go along with 22 points in a 124–120 win over the [[Northern Arizona Suns]].{{cite web|url=https://stats.gleague.nba.com/game/2021900225/|title=South Bay Lakers 124 – Northern Arizona Suns 120|publisher=G-League Stats|date=December 28, 2019|access-date=June 20, 2020}} He suffered a stress reaction in his foot on January 13, sidelining him for several weeks.{{cite news |title=Lakers' Devontae Cacok: Nursing stress reaction in foot |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/lakers-devontae-cacok-nursing-stress-reaction-in-foot/ |access-date=February 2, 2020 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=January 13, 2020}} Cacok returned to action on February 1, contributing 13 points and seven rebounds in a win over the [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]].{{cite news |title=Lakers' Devontae Cacok: Back in action in G League |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/lakers-devontae-cacok-back-in-action-in-g-league/ |access-date=February 2, 2020 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=February 2, 2020}} At the close of the season, Cacok was named to the [[All-NBA G League Team|All-NBA G League First Team]] after averaging 19.4 points, 11.4 rebounds and 1.1 steals per game. He was also named to the League's All-Rookie Team.{{cite news |title=Devontae Cacok Named to All-NBA G League First Team|url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/devontae-cacok-named-all-nba-g-league-first-team|access-date=June 27, 2020 |work=[[NBA.com]] |date=June 26, 2020}} On August 13, he made his NBA debut for the Lakers, scoring six points on 3-of-6 shooting and grabbing five rebounds in a 136–122 loss to the [[Sacramento Kings]].{{cite news |last1=Smist |first1=John |title=Devontae Cacok makes NBA debut |url=https://www.wect.com/2020/08/13/devontae-cacok-makes-nba-debut/ |access-date=August 14, 2020 |work=WECT |date=August 13, 2020}} On September 20, 2021, Cacok signed with the [[Brooklyn Nets]].{{cite web |title=Brooklyn Nets Sign Devontae Cacok |url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/2021/09/20/brooklyn-nets-sign-devontae-cacok |website=NBA.com |access-date=September 20, 2021 |date=September 20, 2021}} He was waived at the end of training camp on October 16.{{cite web |title=Brooklyn Nets Waive Devontae Cacok |url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/2021/10/16/brooklyn-nets-waive-devontae-cacok |website=NBA.com |access-date=October 17, 2021 |date=October 16, 2021}} ===San Antonio Spurs (2021–2022)=== On October 18, the [[San Antonio Spurs]] claimed Cacok off waivers and converted his deal into a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Austin Spurs]].{{cite web|title=Spurs claim Devontae Cacok off waivers|url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/news/spurs-claim-devontae-cacok-waivers|date=October 18, 2021|website=NBA.com|accessdate=October 18, 2021}} On March 4, 2022, the [[San Antonio Spurs]] converted Bologna]] of the [[Lega Basket Serie A]] (LBA) and the [[EuroLeague]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.virtus.it/news/devontae-cacok-e-un-nuovo-giocatore-di-virtus-segafredo-bologna/|title=Devontae Cacok is 24, 2023, after having ousted [[Olimpia Milano]] in the semifinals, Virtus won its [[2023 Italian Basketball Supercup|fourth Supercup]], and the third in a row, defeating 97–60 [[Pallacanestro
